candidates.title: Flow Matching on General Geometries
candidates.abstract_summary: Introduces Riemannian Flow Matching as a simulation-free flow matching framework on manifolds with closed-form target vector fields and geometry-aware premetrics.
candidates.relevance_reason: Foundational RFM paper for the seed profile; it supplies the base geodesic/premetric setup that later TV-rate and geometry-grounded analyses build on.
candidates.notes: Must-read background before extracting cross-paper RFM proof patterns.

candidates.title: Reflected Flow Matching
candidates.abstract_summary: Adds a boundary constraint term to continuous normalizing flows and trains reflected CNFs via a flow-matching objective so trajectories remain within constrained domains.
candidates.relevance_reason: Directly targets constrained-domain flow matching, but uses reflection rather than mirror maps or Student-t heavy-tailed priors.
candidates.notes: Important comparison paper for constrained generation; likely useful for positioning more than proof-pattern transfer.

candidates.title: Gauge Flow Matching: Efficient Constrained Generative Modeling over General Convex Set and Beyond
candidates.abstract_summary: Introduces a gauge mapping that transforms generation over compact convex sets to the unit ball, with strict constraint satisfaction, low generation complexity, and bounded approximation errors.
candidates.relevance_reason: Direct competitor/neighbor to mirror flow matching for constrained domains; useful for comparing mirror maps, reflection, and gauge mappings.
candidates.notes: High priority for related-work and innovation triage because it proposes an alternative geometric transformation.

candidates.title: Mirror Diffusion Models for Constrained and Watermarked Generation
candidates.abstract_summary: Proposes mirror diffusion models that learn diffusion processes in an unconstrained dual space induced by mirror maps, enabling generation on convex constrained sets.
candidates.relevance_reason: Key mirror-map constrained-generation background for the mirror flow matching seed; supplies methodology and comparisons, though in diffusion rather than FM.
candidates.notes: Must-read for mirror-map design lineage and constrained generation positioning.

candidates.title: Neural Approximate Mirror Maps for Constrained Diffusion Models
candidates.abstract_summary: Learns approximate mirror maps and inverses from differentiable distance functions so constrained diffusion models can work with general constraints.
candidates.relevance_reason: Not flow matching, but directly relevant to learned or flexible mirror-map construction for constraints beyond analytic convex sets.
candidates.notes: Good adjacent-method paper if the project explores learned mirror maps for FM.

candidates.title: Error Bounds for Flow Matching Methods
candidates.abstract_summary: Provides deterministic-sampling error bounds for flow matching under an L2 approximation error and regularity conditions on data distributions.
candidates.relevance_reason: A core Euclidean FM error-bound paper repeatedly aligned with the seed profile's learned-velocity and deterministic ODE sampler focus.
candidates.notes: Good source for reusable approximation-error-to-sampling-error proof patterns.

candidates.title: An Error Analysis of Flow Matching for Deep Generative Modeling
candidates.abstract_summary: Presents an end-to-end Wasserstein-2 error analysis for CNFs built on flow matching, including bounded-support target distributions and improvements under target score Lipschitzness.
candidates.relevance_reason: Directly studies generated-distribution convergence for FM and can anchor the Euclidean baseline for the seed papers' geometric extensions.
candidates.notes: Must-read if extracting proof patterns around learned velocity field estimation and W2 convergence.

candidates.title: Geometry-Grounded Flow Matching on Compact Manifolds
candidates.abstract_summary: Provides end-to-end guarantees for Riemannian Flow Matching on compact manifolds, separating statistical, approximation/optimization, and ODE-solver errors.
candidates.relevance_reason: Very close to the Riemannian TV seed paper, but focuses on Wasserstein sampling error and intrinsic-dimension learning rates on compact manifolds.
candidates.notes: Strong must-read for compact manifold FM theory and comparison with TV-rate results.

candidates.title: Riemannian Score-Based Generative Modelling
candidates.abstract_summary: Extends score-based generative modeling to Riemannian manifolds by defining diffusion and reverse processes directly on manifold-valued data.
candidates.relevance_reason: Baseline manifold generative modeling theory cited by RFM work; useful for contrasting diffusion/Brownian simulation difficulties with deterministic RFM.
candidates.notes: Read selectively for background and positioning; proof-pattern transfer may be limited unless comparing diffusion vs ODE samplers.

candidates.title: Polynomial Convergence of Riemannian Diffusion Models
candidates.abstract_summary: Establishes polynomially small step-size guarantees for Riemannian diffusion models in TV distance under L2-accurate score estimates and mild curvature assumptions.
candidates.relevance_reason: Adjacent manifold diffusion theory with TV convergence and geometric proof tools; highly relevant to the seed's TV-rate proof ecosystem.
candidates.notes: Good innovation/background bridge for Riemannian TV proof techniques.

candidates.title: Lipschitz regularity in Flow Matching and Diffusion Models: sharp sampling rates and functional inequalities
candidates.abstract_summary: Develops sharp Lipschitz regularity theory for flow-matching vector fields and diffusion scores, yielding near-optimal Wasserstein discretization bounds for Euler-type samplers.
candidates.relevance_reason: Directly addresses velocity-field Lipschitz regularity and discretization constants, a central bottleneck in the seed profile.
candidates.notes: Very strong candidate for innovation-oriented reading because it targets constants and sharp rates.

candidates.title: The probability flow ODE is provably fast
candidates.abstract_summary: Provides polynomial-time convergence guarantees for the probability-flow ODE implementation of score-based generative modeling using deterministic dynamics plus a corrector step.
candidates.relevance_reason: Adjacent deterministic generative ODE theory with proof tools for noncontractive dynamics and TV-style guarantees.
candidates.notes: Useful for proof-method transfer, especially if seeking polynomial dependence in deterministic ODE samplers.
